page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 8 shared vCPUs, representing 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core, and a substantial memory capacity of 128.0 GB, yielding 16.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the shared nature of the vCPUs. However, multi-core CPU benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU tests, achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register in the average range, though the PassMark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated single-core CPU performance. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it suitable for large-scale caching, in-memory database operations like Redis, and multi-threaded text or image processing. However, it is poorly suited for heavy LLM inference workloads, as demonstrated by below-average text generation speeds on medium-sized models.
